By using an explicit RGBα volume, the method allows for efficient rendering and the application of structural losses, which are not directly applicable to NeRF-like methods due to their sparse ray sampling [S1].

The claim states that using an explicit RGBα volume allows for efficient rendering and the application of structural losses, which are not directly applicable to NeRF-like methods due to their sparse ray sampling. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly supports all parts of this claim: 1) It describes modeling the scene as an 'explicit RGBα volume V' to 'amortize rendering across views' and achieve 'dramatic rendering speed improvements' (efficient rendering). 2) It states that 'One advantage of our formulation is that it supports the use of structural losses like SSIM... and are not directly applicable to NeRF-like methods... as they randomly sample sparse rays from each image during training due to the computational constraints.' This matches the claim's reasoning regarding structural losses and NeRF-like methods.
